title: Batch Allocator for Maintenance Cohorts and Throughput Hedging
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Implement a maintenance cohort allocator service that coordinates node lifecycle operations (cordon/drain/upgrade/reintegrate) across Dedicated fleets while hedging throughput using temporary escrow lanes and autoscaler handshakes. Goal: enable frequent, small maintenance waves with predictable per-tenant throughput guarantees and minimal SLO perturbation. Core responsibilities: compute safe cohort groupings (maintenance cohorts), schedule drain windows, reserve throughput escrow tokens, interface with autoscaler to request burst capacity, and coordinate KV cache prewarm/rehydration before traffic handoff. This ticket covers design, prototype implementation, canary rollout, and post-rollout ops playbook.
non_goals: Replace existing autoscaler core logic (we will only integrate via API)
design_decisions: Use cohort-based batching (groups sized by per-cluster tail-capacity and app contracts) to reduce blast radius
Escrow tokens expressed as virtual throughput reservations tied to app SLAs; refunded after reintegration success
KV prewarm uses a two-phase rehearse+preheat model: rehearsal traffic (sampling) -> targeted KV populate -> full traffic handoff
tradeoffs: Cohort size vs frequency: smaller cohorts reduce SLO risk but increase overall maintenance duration
Escrow reservations temporarily reduce available fill for other waves; use priority-based queue to avoid starvation
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can compute cohorts for a fleet in <300ms for fleets up to 5k nodes
End-to-end maintenance wave (cordon->drain->upgrade->reintegration) using cohorts increases median latency by <5% and p99 by <10% for affected tenants in canary cluster
Autoscaler handshake and escrow allocation succeed or rollback within 120s
KV prewarm reduces cold-KV miss rate by >80% on first reintegrated host
implementation_notes: Expose a stable /v1/maintenance API consumed by fleet-ops and the autoscaler
Persist cohort state to cluster control plane with TTL and idempotency tokens
Metrics: cohort_size, escrow_allocated, escrow_refunded, cohort_duration_ms, kv_preheat_success_rate, maintenance_failures
plan: Phase 1: Design doc + API proto (this ticket)
Phase 2: Proof-of-concept in staging with synthetic load and KV warmup probes
Phase 3: Canary on single Dedicated pool with non-critical tenants
Phase 4: Gradual ramp to 50% of fleets with monitoring and automated rollback triggers
Phase 5: Full rollout and runbook handoff to SRE

risks: Autoscaler race: simultaneous burst requests from multiple cohorts could exceed capacity; mitigation: centralized priority arbiter and soft backoff
State reconciliation complexity after control-plane failover; mitigation: idempotent tokens and leader-lease semantics
Unexpected tenant contract violations if escrow allocation logic misestimates traffic; mitigation: conservative initial multipliers and monitoring
rollout_playbook: Step 0: Enable rehearsal mode (dry-run logging) for 48h
Step 1: Canary wave against low-QPS tenant group; observe metrics for 4h
Step 2: If stable, open to 10% of fleets and enable autoscaler handshake feature flag
Step 3: Monitor KV prewarm success and latency SLOs; abort on sustained p99 > 10%
Step 4: Post-mortem and adjust cohort heuristics based on observed tail patterns
qa_criteria: End-to-end e2e test that simulates cohort drain and reintegration under 2x typical QPS
Chaos test: control-plane leader-failover during cohort operation should not leave fleet in stuck state after 5m
Unit tests for cohortizer heuristics with deterministic seed cases
